headline: Southborough secured a $3.9 million culvert grant, authorized a $105,000 police drone package, and advanced Neary School building plans in June 2026.
synopsis: Southborough municipal boards navigated significant capital and financial decisions throughout June 2026. The town received nearly $3.9 million from the state culvert program, sparing taxpayers from issuing previously approved debt. After extensive debate over funding mechanisms, the Select Board voted 3-2 to approve a $105,000 police drone system using year-end operating surplus. Neary Elementary School advanced on two fronts, executing a $165,000 feasibility contract with Tappe Architects while receiving favorable $2.8 million roof replacement bids. Meanwhile, the Wastewater Study Committee halted a proposed $30,000 Route 9 economic analysis to confirm site viability first, postponing a District Improvement Financing article ahead of the October 17 Special Town Meeting.

top_items.title: Select Board approves $105,000 police drone purchase
top_items.why: The Select Board voted 3-2 to authorize year-end department surplus funds for a five-year drone package.
top_items.body: After initially excluding the drone purchase from year-end spending requests on June 16, the Select Board voted 3-2 on June 29 to approve acquiring a $105,000 Axon outdoor drone package using surplus personnel funds, offset by a $20,000 contribution from Fay School. While the Capital Improvement and Planning Committee endorsed the system as an immediate public safety priority, members debated whether funding major capital programs through operational salary surplus rather than Town Meeting established an unfavorable financial precedent.

top_items.title: State culvert grant saves town $3.9 million in borrowing
top_items.why: Southborough received nearly $3.9 million from the Massachusetts Community Culvert Grant Program.
top_items.body: The Select Board announced that Southborough received nearly $3.9 million in state grant funding for culvert infrastructure replacements. Because Town Meeting had previously approved $3.9 million in borrowing for the work, the grant allows the Department of Public Works to execute the culvert repairs without issuing municipal debt.

top_items.title: Neary Elementary School advances feasibility study and roof project
top_items.why: Tappe Architects began the school building study, while roof bids arrived well under budget at $2.8 million.
top_items.body: The Select Board approved a $165,000 contract with Tappe Architects for the Neary Elementary School feasibility study, followed by a committee kickoff session to outline design options for Town Meeting. Concurrently, the School Committee reported that low bids for the summer Neary roof replacement totaled roughly $2.8 million, well below the $4.5 million authorized by Town Meeting.

top_items.title: Wastewater committee rejects $30,000 Route 9 financial study
top_items.why: The committee voted 0-5 against spending $30,000 on an economic study before verifying site viability.
top_items.body: Although the Select Board approved transferring $30,000 from the Economic Development Committee budget for MassDevelopment consulting, the Wastewater Study Committee unanimously rejected executing the Camoin Associates study. Members determined it was premature to model financial projections before identifying an environmentally viable treatment and disposal site within the Sudbury Reservoir watershed, postponing a District Improvement Financing warrant article for Fall Town Meeting.

top_items.title: Peninsula Trail Phase 2 drops boardwalk, seeks CPA bridge funds
top_items.why: The Trails Committee scaled back its proposal to an estimated $440,000 to $450,000 footbridge over the reservoir.
top_items.body: After combined bids for both a bridge and boardwalk reached roughly $630,000, the Trails Committee decided to drop the boardwalk and reroute the trail across natural upland terrain. The committee finalized an application for Community Preservation Act funding to cover the footbridge and abutments, which earned formal letters of support from both the Conservation Commission and the Recreation Commission.

top_items.title: Southborough Golf Club irrigation estimate approaches $1 million
top_items.why: Higher construction bids and a required booster pump station raised the project estimate to roughly $900,000.
top_items.body: The Golf Committee and DPW reviewed adjusted costs for the golf course irrigation system with the Community Preservation Committee. While value engineering reduced scope by approximately $160,000, engineers determined that adding a booster pump station will cost $200,000, bringing total projections close to $900,000 and prompting discussions over using golf revolving funds to bridge the shortfall.

top_items.title: Conservation Commission reviews 32-unit 40B on Turnpike Road
top_items.why: A proposed rental development at 250 Turnpike Road requires local wetland buffer and vernal pool reviews.
top_items.body: Expedited Engineering presented a Notice of Intent on behalf of FD 250 Turnpike LLC for a Chapter 40B development consisting of 32 townhouse-style rental units. Approximately 3.5 acres of the 5.2-acre parcel will be altered, prompting commissioner questions regarding the town's 20-foot no-disturb zone and salamander migration corridors near an onsite vernal pool before continuing the hearing for peer review.
